release.source: Kaggle mirror of SIAK (Say It Again, Kid!) with identifying metadata removed
release.license: CC-BY-ND-4.0 (commercial building/evaluation of speech technology models not prohibited)

annotation.score: single expert annotator, 0-100 (paper maps to 0-5 stars)
annotation.utterance: single word or short phrase (dashes for spaces)

rejected_class_investigation.documented_externally: SLATE 2023 paper (E2): 1,489 items rejected before scoring (silence, interrupted, wrong word, spoken noise, lack of effort)
rejected_class_investigation.evidence: score minimum is 1; zero-rating rows = 0; rejected items are not present as a labeled class

score_1_items.interpretation: rating 1 of 100 = scored as very poor pronunciation, not an explicit rejection; must not be conflated with the paper's rejected class

rejected_class_investigation.conclusion: SIAK provides documented (paper-level) support for a pre-scoring rejection gate, but the released data cannot empirically verify an assessability classifier: no rejected rows, no rejection reason, no zero ratings.

speaker_leakage.official_splits: filenames encode train/test; speaker numbers are disjoint across splits
speaker_leakage.within_split_repeats: each speaker contributes many repetitions of the same targets (e.g., train001 has 420 items over months); any future fine-tuning must hold out speakers, not utterances
